content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Supplier Concentration Risk", "construction": "From 10-K filings, count the number of distinct major suppliers disclosed (firms with concentrated purchasing report reliance on few suppliers). Construct a Herfindahl-style measure using the fraction of cost of goods sold attributable to the top disclosed suppliers; where explicit percentages are unavailable, use a dummy for disclosed dependence on a single supplier providing >10% of inputs. Rank cross-sectionally annually.", "rationale": "Firms dependent on few suppliers bear input-disruption and hold-up risk that is underappreciated and slowly incorporated, commanding a risk premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high supplier concentration"}, {"name": "Order Backlog Momentum", "construction": "Using Compustat data item order backlog (BACKLOG), compute the year-over-year change in backlog scaled by lagged total assets. Form cross-sectional deciles each fiscal year on the change.", "rationale": "Rising order backlog signals accelerating future demand not yet in reported earnings, and investors underreact to this leading indicator of revenue.", "higher_returns_for": "high increase in order backlog"}, {"name": "Deferred Revenue Growth", "construction": "Compute the year-over-year growth in the deferred/unearned revenue balance sheet liability, scaled by lagged total assets. Rank firms cross-sectionally each quarter using the most recent quarterly balance.", "rationale": "Growth in deferred revenue reflects prepaid future sales (a hidden order book), signaling demand strength that the market underweights because it sits in liabilities.", "higher_returns_for": "high deferred revenue growth"}, {"name": "Advertising-to-Sales Surprise", "construction": "Compute advertising expense (Compustat XAD) divided by sales. Regress this ratio on its own industry-year average and firm history; take the residual as the abnormal advertising intensity. Rank cross-sectionally annually.", "rationale": "Abnormally high advertising builds intangible brand capital not capitalized on the balance sheet, leading to underpricing of future cash flows.", "higher_returns_for": "high abnormal advertising intensity"}, {"name": "Effective Tax Rate Volatility", "construction": "Using the last 5 years of annual data, compute the standard deviation of the firm's effective tax rate (total income taxes / pretax income), winsorized to [0,1]. Rank cross-sectionally each year.", "rationale": "Volatile effective tax rates proxy for opaque earnings management and tax-planning uncertainty, generating a risk premium and mispricing.", "higher_returns_for": "high tax rate volatility"}, {"name": "Employee Productivity Trend", "construction": "Compute sales per employee (SALE/EMP) and take its two-year change scaled by the prior level. Rank firms cross-sectionally annually.", "rationale": "Accelerating labor productivity signals operational improvement and operating leverage that is slowly reflected in prices.", "higher_returns_for": "high improvement in sales-per-employee"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Acceleration", "construction": "Compute the second difference (acceleration) in capital expenditures (CAPX) scaled by lagged total assets: (CAPX_t - CAPX_{t-1}) minus (CAPX_{t-1} - CAPX_{t-2}). Rank cross-sectionally annually.", "rationale": "Sharply accelerating investment tends to precede overexpansion and subsequent low returns, capturing empire-building and overinvestment beyond the level of investment.", "higher_returns_for": "low (most negative) capex acceleration"}, {"name": "Inventory-Sales Divergence", "construction": "Compute the difference between year-over-year inventory growth (INVT) and year-over-year sales growth (SALE). Positive values indicate inventory building faster than sales. Rank cross-sectionally annually.", "rationale": "Inventory outpacing sales signals demand weakness and future markdowns, predicting lower returns as the deterioration becomes visible.", "higher_returns_for": "low inventory-sales divergence (inventory growing slower than sales)"}, {"name": "Intra-Year Return Consistency", "construction": "Over the past 12 months, compute the fraction of months with positive returns minus fraction with negative returns, holding total 12-month return roughly constant by residualizing against past 12-month cumulative return. Rank the consistency residual cross-sectionally monthly.", "rationale": "Steady, consistent gainers reflect stable improving fundamentals that continue, whereas lumpy returns reflect one-off events; the market underprices smooth improvers.", "higher_returns_for": "high return consistency"}, {"name": "Pension Funding Change", "construction": "Compute the year-over-year change in pension funded status (fair value of plan assets minus projected benefit obligation, from pension footnotes) scaled by lagged total assets. Rank cross-sectionally annually.", "rationale": "Improving pension funding frees future cash flows and signals reduced hidden leverage that investors are slow to reprice given footnote opacity.", "higher_returns_for": "high improvement in pension funded status"}]}
